one_liner: Rust crate of 4- and 8-lane SIMD Xoshiro256+/++, frand and biski64 generators; about 4.5x scalar rand_xoshiro Xoshiro256+ on AVX-512.
what_it_does: Provides vectorized PRNGs for Rust that return a whole vector of random numbers per call: next_u64x8()/next_f64x8() (and x4 variants) in the portable module built on nightly std::simd, or __m256i/__m512i values in the specific::avx2 and specific::avx512 modules built on intrinsics. Generators implement rand_core's SeedableRng (from_seed, seed_from_u64) but expose their own SimdRandX4/SimdRandX8/SimdRand traits rather than RngCore, so they are not drop-in replacements for a scalar rand RNG. It targets hot loops that already work in SIMD, such as Monte Carlo kernels.
how_it_is_fast: Each lane holds an independent copy of the generator state (multi-stream), so one vector step of xoshiro256+ (add, shift by 17, four XORs, rotate by 45) produces 4 or 8 outputs at once; the scalar xoshiro256+ has a serial state dependency that the compiler does not vectorize. frand (a Weyl increment followed by a multiply-xor-shift mix) is simple enough that the compiler already autovectorizes the scalar crate, so FrandX8 gains only from keeping eight lane states resident instead of broadcasting one state each call.
when_to_use: Rust Monte Carlo or simulation kernels already written with std::simd or AVX2/AVX-512 intrinsics that consume random u64 or f64 vectors
Bulk generation on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 (avx512f+avx512dq) or AVX2 where 8 independent streams are acceptable
Throughput-bound code where the scalar rand_xoshiro Xoshiro256+ is a measured bottleneck
Projects on nightly Rust that want a portable SIMD RNG that also compiles on non-x86 targets
when_not_to_use: C or C++ projects: it is a Rust crate with no C API, so it needs FFI work; use a C++ SIMD xoshiro sibling instead
Code that needs the same sequence as a scalar generator, reproducible jump-ahead between lanes, or lane splitting (lane jumps are a README TODO)
Stable Rust without x86 SIMD: the portable module needs nightly; the specific modules compile only with the matching target features
Statistically critical work: the author says he is no expert and has only run PractRand; no TestU01 results are published
Production use expecting a mature crate: one crates.io release (0.1.0, February 2026, 64 downloads), 7 stars

integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 (MSRV, edition 2024); nightly for the portable feature
integration.platforms: portable: any target with nightly std::simd; specific::avx2: x86-64 with AVX2 (extra paths with avx512dq/avx512vl); specific::avx512: x86-64 with avx512f and avx512dq
integration.thread_safety: not documented; generators are plain owned state with no shared globals, so use one instance per thread

gotchas: FrandX8::seed_from_u64 (portable and AVX-512 versions, and FrandX4) copies one seed into every lane, so all lanes emit the same stream; the README's own benchmark rows use it. Seed with distinct from_seed bytes when you need independent lanes

The crates.io 0.1.0 release (2026-02-01) predates the 2026-03-15 'fix frand implementation (#34)' commit that made FrandX8 match the upstream frand crate; use the git main branch for upstream-identical frand output

The crate uses a fair amount of unsafe for the intrinsics paths, and the specific modules silently vanish if the target features are not enabled at compile time (.cargo/config.toml in the repo sets target-cpu=native)
Results are vectors, not single values; consuming them one element at a time through a scalar API gives back much of the speedup
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it when you are writing Rust and want SIMD xoshiro or frand vectors directly; for C++ the closest siblings are xoshiro8x256pp (8-way xoshiro256++ gist), Xoshiro256PlusSIMD and simdrng, and SHISHUA is faster still if you can switch generator. Romu and Squares are scalar designs, so they suit code that cannot batch.
verified_claims_summary: The author's Criterion run on an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D (unpinned cargo nightly, target-cpu=native plus AVX-512 RUSTFLAGS, LTO, one pinned SMT pair) took 33.1 ns to generate and sum 64 u64 values with scalar rand_xoshiro Xoshiro256+, versus 7.51 ns for the portable Xoshiro256+X8 and 7.08 ns for the AVX-512 version (about 4.4x and 4.7x, derived from page data). For frand the gain over the compiler-autovectorized scalar crate is only about 1.26x (3.18 ns vs 2.53 ns).
status_note: Active (last commit 2026-03-15) but young and lightly used: MIT, 7 stars, one 0.1.0 crates.io release that predates the frand fix; Rust-only, so C++ users would need to port the small generator kernels.
